data.q: What is the file extension for a Blazor component?
data.e: Blazor components use the .razor file extension, which combines Razor markup with C# code.

data.q: Which directive is used to specify the route for a Blazor component?
data.e: The @page directive defines the route template for a component, e.g., @page "/counter".

data.q: How do you declare a parameter in a Blazor component?
data.e: Parameters are declared as properties decorated with the [Parameter] attribute.

data.q: Which lifecycle method is called after a component has finished rendering?
data.e: OnAfterRender (or OnAfterRenderAsync) is called after the component has rendered. OnInitialized runs before first render.

data.q: What is the purpose of the @inject directive in a Razor component?
o: To inject a service from the DI container
data.e: @inject is used to inject services registered in the dependency injection container into a component.

data.q: How do you handle a button click event in Blazor?
data.e: Event handlers in Blazor use the @on{event} syntax, e.g., @onclick="MyMethod".

data.q: Which component is used to define a layout in Blazor?
data.e: LayoutComponentBase is the base class, MainLayout is the default layout component, and LayoutView renders the body in a layout.

data.q: What does the @code block contain in a .razor file?
o: C# code for the component (fields, methods, lifecycle)
data.e: The @code block contains the C# logic for the component, including properties, methods, and lifecycle overrides.

data.q: How do you enable two-way data binding on an input element?
data.e: @bind creates two-way binding. For specific events, use @bind-value:event="oninput".

data.q: Which method is used to trigger a UI refresh after state changes outside of Blazor's event handling?
data.e: StateHasChanged() notifies the component that its state has changed and it needs to re-render.

data.q: What is the purpose of RenderFragment in Blazor?
o: To represent a segment of UI that can be rendered dynamically
To render a component to a string
To fragment the render tree for performance
data.e: RenderFragment represents a delegate that renders a portion of UI, commonly used for child content or dynamic templates.

data.q: How do you define a component that accepts arbitrary child content?
o: Use a parameter named ChildContent of type RenderFragment
data.e: By convention, a parameter named ChildContent of type RenderFragment receives the child content passed to the component.

data.q: Which attribute is used to specify a CSS class conditionally in Blazor?
data.e: You can bind a C# string to the class attribute using class="@myClass" or use classmap for complex conditions.

data.q: What is the difference between Blazor Server and Blazor WebAssembly?
o: Blazor Server runs on the client; WebAssembly runs on the server
Blazor Server runs on the server via SignalR; WebAssembly runs in the browser
Blazor Server uses JavaScript; WebAssembly uses C# only
data.e: Blazor Server executes on the server and communicates via SignalR. Blazor WebAssembly runs compiled C# directly in the browser via WebAssembly.

data.q: How do you navigate programmatically in Blazor?
data.e: Inject NavigationManager and call NavigateTo to change the URL programmatically.

data.q: What is the purpose of the @key directive in a loop?
o: To define a unique identifier for each element to preserve component state
To set the CSS keyframe animation
data.e: @key helps Blazor track items in a list efficiently, preserving component instances and DOM elements when the list changes.

data.q: Which interface must a component implement to participate in forms validation?
o: No interface required; use EditForm and DataAnnotations
data.e: Blazor forms validation uses EditForm with a model and DataAnnotations. No special interface is required on the component.

data.q: How do you call a JavaScript function from Blazor?
data.e: Inject IJSRuntime and use InvokeVoidAsync (or InvokeAsync<T>) to call JavaScript functions from .NET.

data.q: What is the role of the Router component in Blazor?
o: Handles HTTP requests on the server
Matches URLs to components and renders them
data.e: The Router component (usually in App.razor) intercepts navigation and renders the component matching the current URL.

data.q: Which attribute prevents a component from being trimmed during publishing (e.g., for reflection)?
data.e: [DynamicallyAccessedMembers] informs the trimmer about members accessed via reflection, preventing their removal.

data.q: How do you pass a route parameter to a component?
o: @page "/product/{id}" and [Parameter] public int Id { get; set; }
data.e: Define the route template with placeholders in @page and create a matching [Parameter] property (case-insensitive).

data.q: What is the purpose of the CascadingValue component?
o: To cascade CSS styles down the component tree
To pass a value down the component tree without explicit parameters
data.e: CascadingValue allows a value to be available to all descendant components, which can capture it with [CascadingParameter].

data.q: Which method is called when a component receives new parameters from its parent?
data.e: OnParametersSet (or OnParametersSetAsync) is called after parameters are updated, both on initial render and subsequent updates.

data.q: How do you define a generic Blazor component?
data.e: Use @typeparam TItem at the top of the .razor file to declare a generic type parameter for the component.

data.q: What does the @attributes directive do?
o: Applies a dictionary of attributes to an element
data.e: @attributes="myDict" splats a Dictionary<string, object> onto an element, useful for passing arbitrary attributes.

data.q: Which of the following is a built-in Blazor input component for forms?
data.e: InputText, InputTextArea, InputSelect, InputNumber, etc., are built-in components in Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Forms.
